posts.text:
Yemen's government launches an all-out offensive toward the mouth of the Red Sea.

Plus: Ethiopian forces take Mekelle, Quebec's separatists lead at the polls, Brazil heads to a runoff, and Bosnia votes along ethnic lines again.

Five map stories, a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ Yemen's Saudi-backed presidential council announced operations to retake all Houthi-held territory.

Govt forces claim Dhubab district and positions near the Bab al-Mandeb strait, one of the world's key shipping chokepoints.

(BBC, Guardian, Al Jazeera, NYT)

2/ Pro-government forces have taken control of Mekelle, Tigray's regional capital, after rebel forces withdrew, residents told the BBC.

The fighting raises fears of a regional war drawing in Eritrea, Egypt, the UAE and Saudi Arabia.

(BBC, DW, NYT)

3/ Quebec voted Monday with the separatist Parti Québécois leading the polls.

The PQ promises an independence referendum by 2028, three decades after Quebec voted "no" in 1995.

Results weren't in when our sources were compiled.

(Guardian, NYT)

4/ Brazil goes to a runoff on 25 October.

Flávio Bolsonaro, son of ex-president Jair, finished first but below 50%. He faces incumbent Lula, who called the result "unexpected."

(BBC, Guardian, Al Jazeera, DW, NYT)

5/ Bosnia's three-member presidency is set to be dominated by nationalists from all three main ethnic groups, Deutsche Welle reports.

Turnout hit a record low. Same parties, same ethnic lines as the post-1995 map.

(DW)

The data behind it: democracy in 2025 (V-Dem).

Brazil and Canada, this week's big elections, sit in light blue: electoral democracies. Yemen is in the red block covering most of Arabia. Ethiopia is orange.

Data: Our World in Data (CC BY)
